name: RxSwift
verdict_reason: In the only published operator-by-operator comparison, Combine was faster than RxSwift in 10 of 11 tests in release builds; RxSwift won only MapFilterPumping, by 7%. An independent reviewer put the release-build difference at small, with each framework faster in some cases.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmark (neither RxSwift nor Apple) with public test code, but measured in the iOS Simulator under an Xcode beta.
claimed_speedup: RxSwift slower than Combine in 10 of 11 tests (count derived from page data): PublishSubjectPumping 227 ms vs 135 ms, FlatMapsPumping 646 ms vs 367 ms; RxSwift faster only on MapFilterPumping, 123 ms vs 132 ms
workload: RxSwift's own Benchmarks.swift tests translated 1:1 to Combine: subject pumping, map/filter, flatMap, flatMapLatest and combineLatest chains, each for both creation and value pumping, timed with XCTest measure
hardware: MacBook Pro 2018, 2.7 GHz Intel Core i7, 16 GB, running the iPhone XR Simulator
one_liner: Reactive Extensions for Swift; slower than Combine in 10 of 11 published operator benchmarks, so speed is not a reason to pick it.
how_it_is_fast: It is not faster. RxSwift passes every event through class-based observers and disposables, so each operator stage adds reference counting and dynamic dispatch. Combine's publishers are generic value types that the compiler can specialize, which removes some of that per-event overhead.
use_it_when: Supporting OS versions before iOS 13 / macOS 10.15, where Combine does not exist
Linux targets, where Combine is unavailable
An existing RxSwift codebase or a need for operators Combine lacks
skip_it_when: Choosing it for performance over Combine; the published numbers point the other way
New code that can use Combine or Swift concurrency (AsyncSequence)
caveats: Run in the iOS Simulator, where Apple engineers note system components may use untuned implementations
Xcode 11 beta 5 and Combine from 2019; neither framework has been re-measured since
The first published numbers were from debug builds; the README was later updated to release builds, which shrank the gap
The README says Combine 'was faster in every test', but its own table shows RxSwift ahead on MapFilterPumping
Matt Gallagher noted that subscription setup inside the measure block dominates several tests and that he had cases where RxSwift was 3 times faster
tradeoffs: Adds a third-party dependency of several modules (RxSwift, RxCocoa, RxRelay)
Larger binary than using the system Combine framework

evidence.quote: We have updated all the numbers and graphs to use release builds.
Built in Release, those tests show Combine to be slightly faster than RxSwift but not by much.
I have test cases where RxSwift is 3 times faster. I have test cases where Combine is 5 times faster.
